Religious Education
Our mission is to create a community of learners who value and appreciate the diversity of beliefs and cultures represented in our world.
Through our Religious Education curriculum, we aim to foster understanding, respect, and empathy for others, regardless of their religion or background. We believe that by providing students with knowledge and opportunities to engage with different perspectives and traditions, we can build a more inclusive and harmonious society. Through this we aim to equip students with the skills and attitudes necessary to be open-minded, tolerant, and compassionate individuals

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Subjects - The Mill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music
At The Mill, our music curriculum inspires creativity, self-expression and encourages our children on their musical journeys as well as giving them opportunities to connect with others.
At The Mill Primary Academy, our aim is to enable and inspire every child to become a musician; to actively engage with fun and diverse musical experiences. We believe that being a musician requires the self-confidence to be creative and take risks. Children build their knowledge and understanding of the elements of music and develop proficiency, as they nurture their love of and appreciation for music, and achieve personal musical success.
The National Curriculum states that: “As pupils progress, they should develop a critical engagement with music, allowing them to compose, and to listen with discrimination to the best in the musical canon.” Therefore, the foundations of the TKAT music curriculum are underpinned by the technical, constructive and expressive pillars of musicianship, taught through the key concepts of pulse, rhythm, pitch, structure and notation. Children progressively build their understanding of these concepts in order to listen, compose and perform with growing precision and proficiency. Through this, children will make more music, think more musically and become more musical.
Our music curriculum is designed to allow space for exposure, experience and preparation; direct teaching of substantive musical knowledge; mindful practice; and meaningful application as children move their understanding from their conscious to unconscious mind. This, in turn, develops the qualities and characteristics of a rounded musician, ready to continue their musical journey into the next phase of their learning.
At The Mill, we also provide instrumental lessons where children can learn a range of instruments. All children also experience playing recorder, glockenspiels and ukuleles.
Singing is integrated through many subjects in our school. We have weekly singing lessons where we learn about the joy of singing as a group. We also use these sessions to prepare for our KS1 nativity and carol service.
Music development plan summary: The Mill Primary Academy
Music curriculum is blocked throughout the year. This equates to 18 hours of discrete lessons.
Two major musical events each year.
At The Mill we have:
Access to lessons across a range of instruments and voice.
A curriculum that uses untuned instruments and a variety of instruments.
Our own choir that performs twice a year and within the community.
A Rock Steady group.
Strong links with West Sussex Music Services and host a wide-variety of events.
An instrumental room for 1:1 lessons through West Sussex Music Services.

pageCache.text:
The Mill & West Sussex Music Welcome Royal Philharmonic Orchestra Workshop for SEND
We were thrilled to host a wonderfully inclusive musical experience at The Mill Primary Academy as part of a special partnership with West Sussex Music and the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra (RPO)!
On Saturday 28th February, children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), along with their parents and carers, enjoyed a free creative music workshop led by professional musicians from the RPO. The session at The Mill gave participants the chance to explore sound, rhythm and creativity in a welcoming, relaxed environment — with no experience or auditions required.
Open to learners from special schools, mainstream settings and home education, this workshop used inclusive music-making to build confidence, spark curiosity and celebrate creativity.
The event is part of a series of workshops West Sussex Music has been running in collaboration with the RPO, bringing high-quality music experiences directly into our local community.
Thank you to West Sussex Music and the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra for making this inspiring SEND-friendly event possible!

Art & Design
At The Mill, we believe that Art and Design ignite creativity and imagination. Through visual, tactile, and sensory experiences, children gain a unique way of understanding and responding to the world around them.
Art empowers children of all abilities to express what they see, feel, and think, using colour, texture, form, pattern, and a variety of materials and techniques. We inspire them to explore ideas and meanings through the work of diverse artists and designers, encouraging curiosity and critical thinking.
By learning about the roles and impact of art across different times, cultures, and contemporary life, children develop a deeper appreciation of its significance. We believe that the enjoyment and understanding of the visual arts enriches not only their education but their lives as a whole.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths - Subjects - The Mill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Maths
We have adopted the Mathematics Mastery approach to teaching. Mathematics mastery is underpinned by three principles. These are:
Conceptual Understanding - Our pupils deepen their understanding by representing concepts using objects, pictures, symbols and words.
Language and Communication - Our pupils are given opportunities to widen their vocabulary and strengthen their language skills. Maths talk is an important part of every maths lesson.
Mathematical Thinking - We allow our pupils to have opportunities to think mathematically. Throughout the curriculum you will see tasks that require learners to specialise and generalise and to work systematically.
We also have a maths meeting during the day to reinforce key concepts and ensure our children are confident with number and mathematics principles. This starts in Reception and continues up to year six.
Assessing maths – We use NTS tests 3 times a year. This is a national benchmarked test which gives us information on ability and gaps in knowledge which we can then work on filling and plugging to help children reach high standards.

pageCache.text:
RSE
RSE enables our children to become healthy, independent and responsible members of society.
It aims to help them understand how they are developing personally and socially, and tackles many of the moral, social and cultural issues that are part of growing up. We provide our children with opportunities for them to learn about rights and responsibilities and appreciate what it means to be a member of a diverse society. Our children are encouraged to develop their sense of self-worth by playing a positive role in contributing to school life and the wider community.
The documents below detail what is taught in each year group and when.
Autumn 1 Healthy and happy friendships
Autumn 2 Similarities and differences
Spring 1 RSE Caring and responsibility
Spring 2 Families and committed relationships
Summer 1 RSE Healthy bodies healthy minds

Partnerships
At The Mill, we believe in the power of partnership to transform lives and create sustained, long-term impact.
We are incredibly proud to work alongside a wide range of inspiring organisations - locally and nationally - who share our vision of unlocking potential and creating brighter futures. These established partnerships help us provide meaningful experiences, raise aspirations, and open new doors for everyone in our school community.
Enrich learning with real-world connections and opportunities. ensuring that inspiration and relevance are embedded across the curriculum.
Inspire children to dream big and aim high, creating sustained overtime ambition that drives success beyond primary education.
Champion wellbeing and nurture every child's unique journey, through consistently caring relationships and high expectations.
Strengthen our community through shared purpose and collaboration building established links that enhance learning and wellbeing.
Support and empower parents and carers with opportunities to grow and thrive, ensuring this inclusive approach remains embbeded in all we do.
We know that when families are supported, children flourish. That’s why many of our partnerships are designed not only for pupils but for parents and carers too - from skills workshops and family learning sessions to health, wellbeing, and community support. These initiatives are sustained over time, consistently developed and transformationsal in the way they strengthen family engagement.
Each partnership brings something special to our school - and we are deeply grateful for the passion, expertise, and belief in our shared mission.
If you’re an organisation that would like to make a difference alongside us, we’d love to hear from you: office@themill-tkat.org.

pageCache.pageTitle: Writing - Subjects - The Mill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Writing
‘Writing is the painting of the voice’ - Voltaire
We strongly believe that before a child can write, they need to be able to talk through their ideas and confidently use a wide range of vocabulary. We prioritise oracy in our writing sessions and each year group has a unit dedicated to developing children’s ability to speak publicly, for example Year 4 children write, learn, create cue cards and deliver persuasive speeches.
At The Mill, we focus on the purposes for writing and each purpose is taught through a range of genres. Across their writing journey at the school, the children will have opportunities to master writing to:
Talk 4 Writing framework
The three-part Talk 4 Writing model begins with the ‘Imitation’ phase, where children immerse themselves in a model text. Through engaging activities like storytelling and role-play, they develop oracy skills and build confidence as they learn the text's structure and language features.
Next, in the ‘Innovation’ phase, children use their creativity to adapt the model text. This stage encourages them to experiment with new ideas while retaining the core elements of effective writing. Teachers guide children through collaborative writing sessions, fostering a supportive environment that nurtures independence and originality.
Finally, the ‘Invent’ phase allows children to write their own pieces on an area of their choice, drawing on the skills and techniques they've learnt.
Fostering a child’s written voice
In addition to the many opportunities the children are given to create their own written pieces, in the final summer term, the children plan their own writing sessions. This is known as the ‘application term’. Teachers revisit purposes and genres that have been taught across the year and choose one for each of the weeks. The children then have complete say over the content and genre of their writing. This special creative term allows the children the opportunity to demonstrate all that they have learnt in their writing journey at the school so far.
